newsitem.title: USA: Judge approved $11.25 mln settlement vs Edison.
newsitem.headline: Judge approved $11.25 mln settlement vs Edison.

text.p: A U.S. District Judge on Monday approved an $11.25 million discrimination settlement between Edison International's Southern California Edison Co., the United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) and nine African American employees of Edison.

In a statement late Monday, the EEOC said Judge James Ideman approved the agreement calling for the company to create funds totaling $11.25 million to compensate African Americans employed by Edison between January 1, 1989 and May 13, 1996.

Current and former African American employees of Edison may submit claims alleging discrimination occurring between those dates. A claims review has been established to determine if the claims are covered by the settlement. The EEOC said as many as 2,300 employees may be eligible to share in the settlement.
The lawsuit, filed by the nine employees, alleged that African American workers at Edison were denied advancement.

Under the settlement, Edison agreed to review its employment policies to insure they do not result in unlawful discrimination against African Americans or another group of employees. Edison will also conduct diversity training for all of its employees.
